messages:
Carlos (AE): Quick heads-up — European insurer wants an EU-only diagram + proof of key custody and a signed list of subprocessors for the POC. They specifically asked: can we do BYOK for a temporary POC, are logs kept outside EU, and do any analytics vendors (even aggregated) touch raw requests? Need a reply to their vendor-risk person by Monday.
Marta (Security): Short: yes to EU-only. BYOK for a POC is possible on Dedicated and Private (we can accept a wrapped key or provide HSM-backed key import). Hosted can’t accept customer key import today, but we can offer an encrypted, region-scoped CMK managed by Redwood in eu-west-1.
Marta (Security): Logs: default ingestion and logs stay in-region for EU tenants; replication to other regions is opt-in and disabled for EU-only POCs. Retention default is 30 days; we can set to 0 or purge-on-delivery for contracts.
Zoe (Solutions): Minimal ASCII diagram for the one-pager — feel free to copy to a graphic: 
```
User (EU) --> TLS --> Edge (eu-west-1)
  --> Auth service (eu-west-1)
  --> Router -> Inference pool (eu-west-1)
       -> Ephemeral KV cache (in-region)
       -> Results -> return to User
  -> Audit & logs (eu-west-1) [replication: disabled]
Key materials: Redwood CMK (hosted) OR Customer-wrapped CMK (dedicated/private)
```
Zoe (Solutions): Analytics vendors — we run aggregated metrics pipelines. No analytics vendor has access to plaintext inference payloads for EU-hosted customers. We tag rows with a tenant hash and pseudonymize identifiers.
Liam (Product): For the sale: recommend Dedicated POC if they insist on BYOK and signed subproc agreements. Hosted is faster but limited re: BYOK. Also call out fallback behavior: if a GPU pool is unavailable in-region we will not failover to outside EU for an EU-only POC unless customer approves.
Sofia (Legal): We can provide the subprocessor snapshot and a one-off signed attestation for a POC. Note: production subproc changes require the standard 30-day notice; POC snapshot is provided "as of" date and not a contractual update. Also confirm if the insurer requires a separate order form amendment for BYOK.
deploy-bot: Artifact: https://internal.redwood/artifacts/subprocessors/1870018900-snapshot.csv (permissions: sales, legal) :file_folder:
Marta (Security): I'll draft a two-page answers pack: (1) single-page EU-only dataflow (Zoe's ASCII converted), (2) key custody options + step-by-step for BYOK import on Dedicated, (3) logs/retention options, (4) explicit statement re: analytics vendors and no exposure to raw payloads, (5) attached subprocessor CSV. ETA: Friday EOD.
Carlos (AE): Perfect — can you include a short signed attestation line we can attach? The buyer asked for a line they can put in their vendor-risk portal.
Sofia (Legal): I can add a templated attestation: "Redwood Inference confirms that for the EU-only POC (snapshot date), processing and logs are stored in eu-west-1, customer keys remain in-region, and no US-based subprocessors process raw inference payloads." I'll need to review wording with security.
Marta (Security): Sounds good — I'll review and add the BYOK import checklist. Also adding a small note: telemetry traces are sampled and PII is redacted by default; we can disable sampling for the POC if they want no telemetry.
Zoe (Solutions): Once Marta posts the draft, I’ll export the diagram to SVG and a single-page PDF.
Carlos (AE): Action list: Marta draft + attestation by Fri EOD, Zoe PDF diagram post-draft, Sofia review attestation. I'll upload to the insurer portal after legal signs off. Thanks! :raised_hands:
